research_question: Does spatial configuration of conspecific populations across actual islands relate to documented local extirpation beyond source count, isolation, island area, life history and anthropogenic covariates?

source.provider: Consejo Superior de Investigaciones Científicas (Digital.CSIC), 2025 deposition / 2026-06-18 data distribution
source.title: Database of local and global extinct species, biogeographical variables, and biological traits of the Macaronesian vascular flora
source.original_peer_reviewed_paper: Geographic and Biological Drivers Shape Anthropogenic Extinctions in the Macaronesian Vascular Flora, Global Change Biology (2025), DOI 10.1111/gcb.70072

source_announced_tables.S1: documented locally or globally extinct/extirpated Macaronesian vascular taxa
source_announced_tables.S2: island biogeographic and demographic descriptors for islands with extirpations
source_announced_tables.S3_S4: native vascular flora of Azores and Canary islands with extant and extinct taxa, 9 functional traits, study-defined geographic frame

source_preflight.allowed: publisher exact HTTPS workbook and README transport; source SHA256; file length; workbook ZIP integrity, sheet names, nominal Excel dimensions and first-row headers only
source_preflight.prohibited: decoding species occurrence values, extinct/extant response state per taxon/island, source-specific taxon conservation labels or counts, any heldout predictions

criteria_for_future_admission: Unique site and taxon keys and native vs introduced status demonstrable without reading future species response
Local extirpation distinguishable from globally extinct and extant island populations
Historically occupied island species universe and current observed species denominator simultaneously documented, not pseudozeros
At least two separately treated archipelagos with enough source and local extirpation events for a source-aware reference
Temporality of source-island contemporaneous occupancy must be explicitly labelled post-loss, NOT pre-loss predictor
Species-by-island overdispersion and island survey effort/area/human impact are strong baseline controls
Previously published source paper findings are prior art; no recoding as Structural new biological discovery
